festivals: Ras festival / Rash Utsav (annual till 1932; no longer held here)

history.summary: Commissioned by 49th Malla king Bir Hambir (Hambir Malla Dev) in 1600 CE (906 Mallabda). A pyramidal brick monument on a raised laterite plinth (24.5 m square, 12.5 m high), with a central chamber, three vaulted circumambulatory galleries, and hut-like dochala/aatchala turrets; one travel site credits 'Vir Singh', which conflicts with the Bir Hambir attribution. Built to enable mass worship of Radha-Krishna idols brought from across Bishnupur during the Vaishnava Ras festival; the festival was held here annually until 1932, when the Archaeological Survey of India took it over as a Monument of National Importance (also on UNESCO's Tentative list). NOTE: historic brick monument, not an active temple — no regular worship is conducted; ticket counter for the Bishnupur temple complex.

name: Rasmancha
town_description: Bishnupur (Vishnupur) is the historic capital of the Malla kings in Bankura district, West Bengal, famed as a terracotta temple town: its 17th-18th century brick temples, Baluchari sarees, terracotta craft and classical music heritage make it one of the state's best-known heritage destinations.

travel.airport: Nearest airports: Kazi Nazrul Islam Airport, Durgapur (~90 km) and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~140 km)
travel.railway: Bishnupur Junction railway station (in town), well connected to Kolkata
travel.road: ~142 km / ~4 hours by road from Kolkata; state and private buses serve the town
